title: Google Ads Transparency Center: See Competitors’ Google Ads (2026) | Sprites
summary: Use the Google Ads Transparency Center to see competitors’ Google ads in 2026: search by advertiser or domain, filter by format, region and date, plus its limits.
body_markdown:
The **Google Ads Transparency Center** is Google’s public ad library: every ad from every verified advertiser across Search, YouTube, Display and Gmail, searchable by name or website, free, no account required. Since it launched in 2023 it has become the fastest way to check competitors’ Google ads, and in 2026 it also reveals which Search Partner sites a Performance Max campaign is leaning on.


This guide walks through how to use it, what each screen tells you, what it will never tell you, and how to turn a search into a competitor analysis. If you are here from the Facebook side, the companion guide is[how to see competitors’ Facebook ads](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/how-to-see-competitors-facebook-ads) .


## What the Google Ads Transparency Center is


It lives at **adstransparency.google.com** . Google built it after the political-ad transparency reports, and expanded it in 2023 to cover all ads from advertisers who have completed advertiser verification, which is now required for almost every account. Each ad stays in the Center for one year after the last day it was shown; election ads stay for seven years and carry spend and impression ranges that commercial ads do not.


People search for a “Google Ads library” because they expect a mirror of the Meta Ads Library. It is close, with two differences that matter: Google indexes by *verified advertiser* rather than by Page, and it retains ads for a year, where Meta drops ordinary commercial ads the moment they stop outside the EU.


## How to see competitors’ Google ads, step by step


### Step 1: Search by advertiser name or domain


Type the brand into the search bar. The dropdown lists verified advertisers with their legal name and location; pick the right entity. If nothing sensible appears, search the **domain** instead (“example.com”), which returns ads from every advertiser account pointing at that website, including regional subsidiaries and agencies running on the brand’s behalf. Large brands often have several.


### Step 2: The “About this ad” shortcut


When you see a competitor’s ad live on Google or YouTube, open the three-dot menu and choose **About this ad** (or **My Ad Center** ). It names the verified advertiser behind the ad and links straight to their Transparency Center page. This is the fastest route when the legal name differs from the brand.


### Step 3: Set region, format and date


Three filters sit above the results. **Region** limits to ads shown in a country; leave it on anywhere for the global view. **Format** separates text, image and video, which in practice separates Search, Display and YouTube. **Date** defaults to the last 30 days, with presets for today and the last seven days and, since late 2025, custom ranges. Widen it to a year to see seasonality.


### Step 4: Read the ad cards


Each card shows the creative, the format, and the last date it was shown. Click through for the full detail: every headline and description variation for a responsive search ad, the video for YouTube, the regions where it ran, and for Performance Max and Display, the “When and where ads showed” panel, which since 2026 lists individual Search Partner domains. That panel tells you whether a competitor’s PMax spend lands on reputable placements or on long-tail filler sites.


### Step 5: Record and compare


The Center has no export, no side-by-side view and no alerts. Copy the headlines, note the landing pages and formats, and keep a sheet per competitor, or use an ad library that does this for you (below).

## What the Transparency Center will never show you


- **Keywords and bids.** You see the ad, not the query that triggered it. Infer themes from headlines and landing-page URLs.
- **Spend, impressions, clicks, conversions.** Published for election ads only.
- **Targeting.** No audiences, no demographics, no schedules.
- **Shopping ads.** Product listing ads are not in the Center.
- **Unverified advertisers.** Rare now, but their ads are not listed under a name.
- **Ads older than a year.** Retention is twelve months from last shown.


Two sources fill part of the gap. **Auction Insights** inside your own Google Ads account shows, per campaign or keyword, which advertisers compete with you, their impression share, overlap rate and how often they outrank you; it is the only place you see competitor presence on *your* keywords. And an ad library such as[Sprites](https://www.sprites.ai/ads-library) adds run length, launch tempo, destination analysis and an estimated spend range calculated from the public data and labelled as an estimate.


## A competitor Google ads analysis in six checks


1. **Headline inventory.** List every headline asset across their search ads. The claims that appear in every ad are the ones they have proven; the ones that appear once are tests.
2. **Offer and price.** Do they name a price, a discount, a free trial, a guarantee? An offer in the headline means they compete on it.
3. **Landing pages.** Group ads by destination URL. One page for everything means message testing; many pages means segmented campaigns by product or audience.
4. **Format spread.** Search only, or Search plus YouTube plus Display? Video and Display presence signals budget beyond bottom-funnel capture.
5. **Seasonality.** Set the date range to a year and watch what appears and disappears. Ads that return every quarter are working; ads that vanished after two weeks were not.
6. **Partner quality.** For PMax advertisers, read the Search Partner domains panel. Filler placements suggest they are buying cheap reach; premium placements suggest a brand budget.


Repeat for three competitors and the map of the category is clear: who owns which claim, who segments and who does not, and which angle nobody is running.

## Frequently asked questions


### Is there a Google Ads library like the Facebook Ad Library?


Yes. Google calls it the Ads Transparency Center, at adstransparency.google.com. It shows the ads of every verified advertiser across Search, YouTube, Display and Gmail, searchable by advertiser name or website, with filters for format, region and date. It is free and needs no Google account.


### How do I see what Google ads my competitors are running?


Open adstransparency.google.com, type the competitor’s brand name or domain, and pick the verified advertiser. Filter by region and format, and set the date range to cover the period you care about. Each ad card shows the creative, the format, the regions it ran in and the last date it was shown. Click any ad for the full detail.


### Can I see competitors’ keywords in the Google Ads Transparency Center?


No. The Center shows the ads, not the keywords, bids or targeting behind them. You can infer themes from headlines and landing pages, and Auction Insights inside your own Google Ads account shows which advertisers compete with you on the keywords you bid on. Paid tools such as Semrush and SpyFu estimate competitor keywords from search data.


### Does the Google Ads Transparency Center show ad spend?


Only for election ads, which carry spend and impression ranges. For ordinary commercial ads there are no spend, impression, click or conversion figures. Run length, ad volume and regional coverage are the proxies available, and the Sprites Ads Library adds an estimated spend range calculated from public data.


### How far back does the Google Ads Transparency Center go?


Ads from verified advertisers stay in the Center for one year after the last day they were shown; election ads stay for seven years. The date filter defaults to the last 30 days, with presets for today and the last seven days, and custom date ranges added in late 2025.


### Why can’t I find an advertiser in the Transparency Center?


Three usual reasons. The advertiser is not verified, so its ads are not listed under a name (try the domain instead). The legal advertiser name differs from the brand, in which case use About this ad on any live ad to jump to the right entity. Or the ads ran outside the date range and region you have set.


### What is the best way to check competitors’ Google ads regularly?


Bookmark each competitor’s Transparency Center page and check it monthly, or use an ad library that does the reading for you. The Sprites Ads Library keeps one page per advertiser with their Google search headlines, destinations and markets alongside their Meta and LinkedIn ads, and the Sprites copilot can run the comparison on a schedule and report only what changed.
